name: Gulfstream GIV / GV / G450 / G550
summary: Classic large-cabin Gulfstreams; the GV/G550 serves as the USAF/Navy/Army/Coast Guard C-37A/B VIP transport and the EA-37B Compass Call electronic-attack platform.

wings: Low swept wing with upturned winglets
engines: Two Rolls-Royce turbofans (Tay on GIV/G450, BR710 on GV/G550) in long nacelles on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Long, slim fuselage with large oval windows (six per side on GIV/G450, seven on GV/G550)
tail: T-tail with a tall swept fin

tellTales: Row of large oval windows along a long, slim fuselage
T-tail and upturned winglets on a big twinjet
Long, slender engine nacelles on the rear fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The GIV/G550 has a slimmer fuselage, smaller ovals and a pointed nose; the G650/G700 is fatter with bigger ovals, a blunter rounded nose and a more swept wing.
The Gulfstream has oval windows; the Global has rounded-rectangle windows on an even longer fuselage.
The Gulfstream is longer and slimmer with oval windows; the Challenger 600-series has a short, fat wide-body fuselage with rounded-rectangle windows.
The GIV/G550 is a much larger long-range jet with longer nacelles and more windows; the G280 is a short super-midsize.

usCount.source: Gulfstream production (~1,700 GIV/G450/GV/G550) with ~50% active US-registered per JETNET fleet summaries, plus ~40 military C-20/C-37/EA-37B (approx.)
